partners.diseaseBName: inclusion body myopathy with early-onset Paget disease with or without frontotemporal dementia 2
partners.mechanism_chain: MTAP (HGNC:7430) —DISRUPTS→ Methionine adenosyltransferase pathway (REACT:R-HSA-194271); Methionine adenosyltransferase pathway (REACT:R-HSA-194271) —LEADS_TO→ Bone Malignancy (HP:0002671); HNRNPA2B1 (HGNC:4827) —DISRUPTS→ RNA Binding and Processing (GO:0003723); RNA Binding and Processing (GO:0003723) —LEADS_TO→ Paget Disease of Bone (HP:0003301); RNA Binding and Processing (GO:0003723) —LEADS_TO→ Frontotemporal Dementia (HP:0001239). Loss-of-function mutations in MTAP disrupt methionine metabolism, impacting cellular homeostasis and potentially contributing to bone malignancy. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in HNRNPA2B1 impair RNA binding and processing, leading to phenotypes such as Paget disease of bone and frontotemporal dementia. The convergence occurs at the level of cellular processes affected by both genetic disruptions: altered metabolic byproducts from MTAP deficiency and aberrant RNA processing from HNRNPA2B1 deficiency can synergistically impact cellular health and lead to overlapping pathological outcomes.

partners.mechanism_chain: TALDO1 (HGNC:11563) —DISRUPTS→ fructose-6-phosphate (CHEBI:17700); fructose-6-phosphate (CHEBI:17700) —LEADS_TO→ Pentose Phosphate Pathway (GO:0006094); Pentose Phosphate Pathway (GO:0006094) —LEADS_TO→ Bone Malignancy (HP:0002678); Pentose Phosphate Pathway (GO:0006094) —LEADS_TO→ Transaldolase Deficiency (HP:0031821); MTAP (HGNC:7570) —DISRUPTS→ S-adenosylhomocysteine (CHEBI:16787); S-adenosylhomocysteine (CHEBI:16787) —LEADS_TO→ Methionine Metabolism (GO:0006569); Methionine Metabolism (GO:0006569) —LEADS_TO→ Pentose Phosphate Pathway (GO:0006094). Concurrently, mutations in MTAP, which is in close proximity and often co-deleted with the CDKN2A/B locus, lead to the accumulation of S-adenosylhomocysteine, a potent inhibitor of methyltransferases. This accumulation can indirectly disrupt cellular methylation patterns and metabolic processes, including those within the pentose phosphate pathway, potentially converging on shared downstream pathways that contribute to bone malignancy phenotypes seen in diaphyseal medullary stenosis-bone malignancy syndrome. Thus, while TALDO1 is directly implicated in transaldolase deficiency, its downstream effects on the pentose phosphate pathway and the indirect impact of MTAP dysfunction on related metabolic networks create a shared mechanistic overlap.
